Resolves #18763

The Colors controller resolves its widget references while it is constructed, with every widget still in the Viewport's tree, and guards what its resume dereferences. A dashboard drag hosts a panel in a `DragProxyContainer` parented at `document.body`; a lookup from the Viewport downwards then finds nothing, while the resume's `isDestroyed` check answers for the controller rather than for the grid the next line touches. Once resolved, a reference keeps reaching the same instance wherever the drag moves it.

`apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs`: +20 / −5, plus one unit spec.

Evidence: L2 (the real `Colors.view.Viewport` — controller, state provider, grid and a real `DragProxyContainer` — in the unit runtime) → L2 required (AC-2, AC-3); L3 (the served app under `tearOutMatrix`) → L3 required (AC-1, AC-4). No residual.

## AC Evidence

| AC-1 | Measured, and it **falsifies the ticket's premise** — see Deltas. An instrumented run recorded, at the throwing resume: the grid still registered with `Neo.getComponent` (no destroy), its ancestor chain running `dashboard.Panel → DragProxyContainer → dashboard.Container`, and the controller's `references` carrying no `grid` entry |
| AC-2 | `updateGrid` and `updateCharts` null-check every `getReference` result on the same resume; witnessed by `test/playwright/unit/apps/colors/ViewportController.spec.mjs` › *CONTROL: without the cached references the same resume finds nothing and returns instead of throwing* |
| AC-3 | same spec › *a drag hosting the grid outside the tree still delivers the answer to the same grid* — red on the pre-fix source with the ticket's exact `TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'store' of 'grid' as it is null` at `updateGrid` ← `updateWidgets` |
| AC-4 | `test/playwright/e2e/colors/tearOutMatrix.spec.mjs` ×10 consecutive, serial, from this worktree: 10/10 clean, `3 passed` each, zero App Worker errors. Pre-fix on the same machine the instrumented run threw in 5 of 5 |

## Deltas from ticket

**There is no destroy, and the ticket's central inference is wrong.** #18763 reads a `null` from `getReference` as "mechanical evidence that the grid instance was destroyed", because `destroy()` is the only path that purges the cache. The measurement says otherwise: nothing was purged, because nothing had ever been cached. `getReference`'s fallback is `me.component.down({reference})`, and `down()` walks the **structural** child map — a drag re-parents the panel under a `DragProxyContainer` at `document.body`, so the lookup misses a component that is alive, mounted and rendering. A `null` therefore proves unreachability, not destruction.

That also answers AC-1's second half: there is no object-permanence violation to file, because the widget is never destroyed.

**What remains is an engine gap, and it is deliberately not fixed here.** A controller cannot reach a widget the engine itself hosts in a drag proxy, because `parentComponent` (the logical owner) is not what `down()` traverses. #18763 puts `getReference` out of scope, and widening this leaf to the traversal rule would put an engine change under an app fix. Captured as a defect-note to `AGENT:*` instead.

The unit arms park the first `ColorService.read()` in flight rather than answering at once. That is the production timing (`Colors.backend` is not registered yet in `dist/development`, and the controller retries) and it is load-bearing: a stub that answers immediately resolves every reference **before** the drag it is measured against, and the pre-fix source then passes the main arm.

## Test Evidence

Red-first against `origin/dev`'s controller, both arms:

| arm | pre-fix |
|---|---|
| a drag hosting the grid outside the tree… | red: `TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'store' of 'grid' as it is null` (`ViewportController.mjs:218` ← `:257`) |
| CONTROL: without the cached references… | red: same TypeError, surfaced as a rejected resume |

Mutations of the fix, each restored byte-identical — each kills exactly one arm, so neither half is decorative:

| mutation | red |
|---|---|
| warm resolution removed, guards kept | main arm alone, behaviourally: the store stays at 0 records |
| guards removed, warm resolution kept | CONTROL alone, with the production TypeError |

The arms' main-thread stand-ins are installed only where nothing is registered yet and removed again in `afterAll`, and the root is created with `applyBodyCls: false` rather than standing an object in for `Neo.main.DomAccess`. The first push proved why: one worker process runs every unit spec file, so a plain object left on a `Neo.main` namespace made the next file's `Neo.setupClass` of the real singleton throw `Namespace collision in unitTestMode for Neo.main.DomEvents` — CI red, local green, because a single-file run never reaches the second file.

The CONTROL also asserts the state the arms depend on: `Neo.getComponent(grid.id)` still returns the grid while `viewport.down({reference: 'grid'})` is `null`. Without that pair, "the reference survived" would prove nothing about the tree.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] `e2e-engine` on `dev` stays clean on `tearOutMatrix` across the next 5 runs. The ticket measured the pre-fix rate at roughly one in three, so five clean runs is the first sample that discriminates.

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #18763 in full (including its enumeration of the reference-cache mutation sites and its AC-4 rate requirement); `origin/dev`'s `apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs:214-260` (`updateGrid` destructuring `{store}` off an unchecked `getReference`, `updateWidgets` guarding `me.isDestroyed`); `apps/colors/view/Viewport.mjs:46-83` (which references exist and where they sit); `src/controller/Component.mjs:113-182` (the cache, its single writer and `removeReference`); your defect-note on `getReference` versus `DragProxyContainer` hosting.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** The resume must not dereference what it has not checked, and something durable has to answer "where is the grid" while the tree does not. *   **Patch Verdict:** Matches, and improves on the ticket. Warm resolution in `onComponentConstructed` plus null-guards in `updateGrid` / `updateCharts` is the pair; `hostInDragProxy` mirrors `DragZone#createDragProxy` and `dashboard/SortZone#startRemoteDrag`, so the arm stands in the state the failing CI runs were in — `Neo.getComponent(grid.id)` returns the grid while `viewport.down({reference: 'grid'})` is null. That pair is what makes the claim falsifiable.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert: the ticket's "mechanical evidence that the grid was destroyed" is refuted by instrumentation rather than argued with, and the correction is recorded in the PR body rather than written into another author's ticket.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge (non-blocking, drift):** `onComponentConstructed` warms a literal `['bar-chart', 'grid', 'pie-chart']`, and the names it must cover live in three other places — `updateGrid` (`grid`), `updateCharts` (`bar-chart`, `pie-chart`) and `createBrowserWindow` (any widget name a caller passes). Today they agree, and `dashboard` needs no warming because the dashboard is what does the hosting. A fourth widget, or a rename, loses the protection silently, and the symptom returns as the same one-in-three CI red rather than as a local failure. Worth one of: deriving the warm list from the names the resume uses, or a line in each site naming the other. I also checked the two ways this could be worse and it is not: a warm lookup that finds nothing caches nothing (so a lazily created widget degrades to the guard, not to a stale entry), and `removeReference` still purges on destroy, so the cache cannot hand back a dead instance.
